dossier.icp: This is the person awake at 2:07am with the old thread open. Most often a woman, 24–40, somewhere between two weeks and six months past a breakup she has not accepted — composed by day, forensic by night, re-reading messages like evidence. Every friend has already told her to move on, which is exactly why she can't admit out loud that she doesn't want to; she is starving for an authority that takes the wanting seriously instead of pathologizing it, and tells her the one right thing to DO with it. The male respondent is a meaningful minority and he is the same person with fewer witnesses: he has told no one he's searching "how to get her back", he is prouder, more contact-locked ("I can't be the one to text first"), less interested in being understood than in being handed a plan. Both are done with sympathy. They do not need convincing that the ex matters — they need someone to convert the obsession into a concrete next move that doesn't cost them their self-respect. That conversion is the product.
pains: Drafting the perfect "casual" text at 1:47am, reading it three times, deleting it — then checking if {he}'s online anyway.
Watching {his} story within a minute of it posting, then spending an hour wishing you could un-watch it.
Friends saying "you deserve better" when the only thing you actually want is to be told how to get {him} back.
Replaying the last conversation and editing your own lines, as if better words that night would have changed the ending.
The drop in your chest when the phone buzzes and it's anyone but {him} — and the shame of how fast you checked.
Googling your two zodiac signs' compatibility at 2am, closing the tab, and opening it again ten minutes later.
hooks: The cards won't promise your ex back. They'll tell you what to do next. — Honesty as pattern-interrupt: disarms scam radar while centering DO; recommended winner for cold traffic.
There's a text you keep almost sending. The cards know which one — and say wait. — Mirrors the exact 2am behavior (draft-and-delete); unsettlingly specific, implies the deck prescribes.
Find out what the cards tell you to do to win your ex back. — The owner's original: cleanest desire statement, strongest for warm/search intent; benchmark control.
The cards still see a door. Ask them what they want you to do about it. — Possibility frame ('a door, not a promise') plus instruction frame; tests hope-led vs. desire-led entry.
Silence, one message, the right night — the cards lay out your next move. — Previews the actual prescription; makes 'the deck tells you what to DO' tangible before the quiz.

quiz_beats.measures: How long since it ended — rawness vs. entrenchment. Two weeks needs a different prescription than eight months; it also calibrates how much silence the deck can ask for.
quiz_beats.why_seen: Nobody has asked them to place it precisely. Saying 'six weeks' to the cards makes the limbo real — and being asked implies the answer changes the reading, which it does.

quiz_beats.measures: Wound geometry and guilt-holder: blowup, slow fade, mutual-but-not-really, {he} left without a real reason, or they ended it and regret it. This is the primary input for the pattern diagnosis.
quiz_beats.why_seen: The options name endings people believe are uniquely theirs. Finding your exact ending on a list is the first 'how did it know' moment.

quiz_beats.measures: The live channel: still talk sometimes / seen-not-answered / total silence / blocked / watching from a distance. Determines how much room the deck has to prescribe an actual move.
quiz_beats.why_seen: Admitting 'we don't speak but I watch {his} stories' to a deck feels safer than to a friend. The quiz absorbs the confession without flinching or judging.

quiz_beats.measures: Locus of self-blame: I held on too tight / I went cold / I said the thing I can't take back / I honestly don't know — and that's the worst part. Feeds the pattern and tells Aura what to absolve vs. what to correct.
quiz_beats.why_seen: It is the question they ask the ceiling every night, finally asked back — with 'I don't know' offered as a legitimate answer instead of a failure.

quiz_beats.measures: Evidence vs. pure longing: {he} still watches everything I post / the last thing {he} said / a dream that felt like a message / no evidence, just a certainty in my body. Calibrates how honest the possibility-read must be.
quiz_beats.why_seen: It dignifies the irrational signal they've told no one about. Being asked 'what makes you feel it isn't over' assumes the feeling is data, not delusion.

quiz_beats.measures: Commitment to the offer frame: if the cards asked for nine days of silence, or told you NOT to send the message you've drafted — could you do it? Segments compliers from venters and primes 'this deck prescribes.'
quiz_beats.why_seen: It is the first question that treats them as someone about to act rather than someone to be pitied. The implicit respect ('the cards may ask something hard of you') is the conversion moment.

patterns.label: The Unfinished Door
patterns.essence: It ended before the conversation did — what was never said holds the door ajar from both sides, and {he} feels the draft too.

patterns.label: The Pride Standoff
patterns.essence: Neither of you stopped feeling it; you both stopped reaching first. The bond didn't break — the signal did, and someone has to be strong enough to send one.

patterns.label: The Slow Dimming
patterns.essence: Nothing broke it; routine starved it. What dimmed by neglect can't be relit with words — only with change {he} can see without being told to look.

patterns.label: The Storm Exit
patterns.essence: The ending was louder than the love — words bigger than the feeling behind them. The cards ask whether the noise or the bond gets the last word.

moves: The nine-day silence: the deck asks for it not as a game but as a reset — so your next word to {him} isn't an echo of the last argument. The cards see the door after the quiet, not before it. A window, not a guarantee.
The message you don't send: write the 2am paragraph — all of it — and keep it. The cards say {he} was never meant to read it. You needed to say it; you never needed {him} to see it.
Close the watching: no more stories, no more last-seen, no more new photos. The cards can't read a door in a room you keep haunting — and {he} can feel the watching more than you think.

Show up changed before you show up at all: one real, visible shift in your own life — the thing {he} used to ask of you, done for yourself now. The cards see the door opening for who you're becoming, not who {he} left.

If the cards open first contact: one light line with no question inside it — a memory, a congratulation, something true. Nothing that reopens the case. Then let it breathe; the deck reads what follows as information, not defeat.

If {he} reaches first: wait one breath, answer warm and short, and end the exchange one message earlier than you want to. The cards favor the one who leaves the room still lit — that is where they see the window widen.

objections.honest_a: No one can promise you that — not a deck, not a psychic, not even {him}. What the cards can do is read whether a door is still open and tell you which move gives it its best chance without costing you your dignity. It's a window, not a guarantee. Anyone who promises the return is selling you the promise, not the truth.

objections.q: What if the cards say it's really over?
objections.honest_a: Sometimes they do. Master Aura won't dress a closed door as an open one — you'll be told plainly, and the moves the deck gives you will shift to what protects and rebuilds you instead. Either way, the guessing ends tonight, and that's the part that's been eating you.

objections.q: Is this going to be games — jealousy, playing hard to get?
objections.honest_a: No. The deck never prescribes anything you'd be ashamed of later. Silence to heal, not to punish. No jealousy bait, no fake accounts, no scripts that make you smaller. If a move would cost you your self-respect, it isn't in the reading — the cards want {him} to meet someone worth returning to.

objections.q: How is this different from a free tarot app?
objections.honest_a: A free spread hands everyone the same card meanings. This reading is built from your answers — how it ended, where contact stands right now, the pattern running between you two — and it ends in instructions, not vibes. 120,000+ readings delivered, rated 4.9. And it still won't promise you {him} back; that honesty is exactly why you can trust the rest of it.
